findings.quote: Set two expressions equal only when they label opposite (vertical) angles.
findings.problem: B01: The word "only" makes this rule false. When two lines are perpendicular, adjacent angles both measure 90 degrees, so their expressions can also be set equal. Students applying this rule would reject a valid equation.
findings.source: [OpenStax, Elementary Algebra 2e, Section 4.5: perpendicular lines](https://openstax.org/books/elementary-algebra-2e/pages/4-5-use-the-slope-intercept-form-of-an-equation-of-a-line). Perpendicular lines form right angles, so adjacent angles at their intersection are equal.
